title: Liquid-metal bundle mixing during flow transition
open: Predict subchannel redistribution and local temperature maxima as a heated pin bundle changes from forced to buoyancy-driven circulation. Validate asymmetric heating, conjugate wall conduction, and interchannel mixing together, including conditions outside uniformly heated benchmarks.
status: Batta and Class (2024 online; 2025 issue) obtained good CFD agreement for the uniformly heated NACIE-UP benchmark. Transfer to asymmetric and transient cases remains a separate validation task.
why: Bundle-average flow can conceal poorly cooled individual channels.
key_works: A. Batta and A. G. Class (2024/2025), *CFD Validation of Forced and Natural Convection for the Open Phase of IAEA Benchmark CRP-I31038*, [DOI:10.1007/s13369-024-09480-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13369-024-09480-x).

title: Flashing-induced natural-circulation instability
open: Predict transitions between steady circulation, intermittent flashing, and sustained two-phase oscillation from loop geometry and thermal history. Determine how delayed nucleation and compressible vapor volumes alter onset and recovery, validating the criterion across facilities.
status: Fang, Cao, and Tian (2025) experimentally mapped multiple flashing regimes in an open loop. A geometry-transferable stability boundary remains open.
why: Passive cooling can oscillate even when its average driving head appears adequate.
key_works: Y. Fang, X. Cao, and W. Tian (2025), *Experimental Study On Flashing-Induced Instabilities In An Open Natural Circulation System*, [arXiv:2506.06213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06213).

title: Condensation with mixed noncondensable gases
open: Predict condensation when steam mixes with gases of different diffusivities and buoyancies in passive cooling tubes. Demonstrate transfer among tube sizes and changing gas inventories, including whether helium surrogates adequately represent hydrogen-containing mixtures.
status: Bhowmik’s openly released 2024 dataset covers several tube diameters and helium or nitrogen admixtures. Multicomponent, dynamically evolving mixtures remain a stronger target than these separate tests.
why: Accumulated noncondensables can reduce passive heat-removal capacity.
key_works: P. Bhowmik (2024), *Test dataset for “Steam condensation scaled experiment in the presence of non-condensable gases for small modular reactor containment passive safety”*, [DOI:10.5281/zenodo.14090025](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14090025).

title: Reflood quench fronts in deformed bundles
open: Predict quench-front movement, droplet entrainment, and rod temperatures during reflood when cladding deformation changes local flow passages. Validate deformation effects independently of adjustments already fitting undeformed-bundle heat transfer.
status: RBHT-II and ISP-53 held final meetings in March 2026, comparing open and blind calculations for undeformed and deformed bundles. Robust transfer between geometries remains the research target.
why: Emergency cooling performance depends on the damaged geometry that cooling encounters.
key_works: OECD NEA (2026), [*RBHT II and ISP 53 participants conclude final project meetings*](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_116670/rbht-ii-and-isp-53-participants-conclude-final-project-meetings).

title: Quantified scaling distortion in integral experiments
open: Infer full-plant transients from facilities that cannot simultaneously preserve gravitational, thermal, interfacial, and wall-storage similarity. Use counterpart tests to separate scaling distortion from code error, validating uncertainty on a facility withheld from calibration.
status: The NEA ATLAS project has operated since 2014. Its 2025–2028 phase retains counterpart testing and questions concerning low driving forces and asymmetric flows.
why: Agreement at one experimental scale does not establish accuracy at plant scale.
key_works: OECD NEA (2025–2028), [*Advanced Thermal-hydraulic Test Loop for Accident Simulation (ATLAS) Project*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_24812/advanced-thermal-hydraulic-test-loop-for-accident-simulation-atlas-project).

title: Corium thermophysical-property uncertainty
open: Establish traceable density, viscosity, surface-tension, and phase-boundary data for representative evolving corium compositions. Quantify measurement and compositional uncertainties sufficiently to propagate them through melt-stabilization calculations.
status: The NEA COPS project began in April 2024 and runs to April 2029, targeting measurements for 40 compositions and complementary integral experiments. Initial composition tests began in 2024.
why: Property uncertainty propagates into spreading, stratification, and cooling predictions.
key_works: OECD NEA and CEA (2024–2029), [*COPS: The COrium Properties for reactor Simulation and uncertainties*](https://www.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_100417/cops-the-corium-properties-for-reactor-simulation-and-uncertainties-cops).

title: Transient corium stratification and heat focusing
open: Predict maximum vessel-wall heat loading while melt progressively arrives, incorporates structural material, and exchanges species between oxide and metal layers. Resolve whether transient stratification or inversion produces peaks missed by steady-state configurations.
status: Carénini et al. (2025) compared eight IAEA benchmark cases and documented remaining thermochemistry, heavy-metal-layer, debris-melting, and heat-transfer discrepancies after decades of retention research.
why: Demonstrating melt retention requires bounding transient heat loads.
key_works: L. Carénini et al. (2025), *IVMR modelling with transient effects during molten pool formation and stabilization—Outcomes from models’ comparison performed in the IAEA CRP J46002*, [DOI:10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111365](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111365).

title: Directional corium–concrete erosion
open: Predict the evolving split between lateral and downward concrete erosion from melt composition, concrete chemistry, gas generation, and crust structure. Validate across siliceous and carbonate-bearing concretes under dry and flooded conditions.
status: The MCCI programme and its 2017 synthesis established substantial integral evidence. Orientation-dependent erosion and extrapolation among compositions remain sources of uncertainty.
why: Erosion geometry determines cooling surfaces and progression of structural attack.
key_works: OECD NEA (2017), [*State-of-the-Art Report on Molten Corium Concrete Interaction and Ex-Vessel Molten Core Coolability*](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_19746/state-of-the-art-report-on-molten-corium-concrete-interaction-and-ex-vessel-molten-core-coolability).

title: Coolability of heterogeneous debris and spreading melts
open: Predict when water can penetrate and cool heterogeneous debris or spreading, crust-forming melt before an impermeable hot region persists. Relate segregation, porosity evolution, metal content, and melt–water contact to a validated cooling limit.
status: ROSAU completed five debris/coolability and five spreading experiments by the end of 2024 and improved CORQUENCH and MELTSPREAD. Reactor-scale and new-material extrapolation remain open.
why: Stabilization depends on internal cooling pathways as well as water availability.
key_works: OECD NEA and Argonne National Laboratory (2019–2024), [*Reduction of Severe Accident Uncertainties (ROSAU) Project*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_25254/reduction-of-severe-accident-uncertainties-rosau-project).

title: Ex-vessel melt–water interaction bounds
open: Establish validated conservative bounds on mechanical loading from accidental melt–water interactions, accounting for uncertain fragmentation, solidification, and vapor distribution. Determine which laboratory-to-plant extrapolations remain valid for realistic multicomponent melts.
status: SERENA (2002–2012) substantially improved experimental and modeling understanding. Its assessment did not eliminate ex-vessel concerns; closure and scaling uncertainties remain.
why: Robust bounds support protective structures and mitigation without relying on one best-estimate interaction history.
key_works: OECD NEA (2014), [*Steam Explosion Resolution for Nuclear Applications (SERENA) Project*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_25786/steam-explosion-resolution-for-nuclear-applications-serena-project).

title: Recombiner performance in chemically complex atmospheres
open: Predict passive hydrogen-recombiner removal rates under mixed gases, aerosols, oxygen limitation, and catalyst poisoning. Validate degradation and recovery under changing accident atmospheres.
status: THEMIS completed targeted tests by 2023 and an integral aerosol–recombiner interaction test in 2024; mixture and exposure-history transfer remains open.
why: Catalytic mitigation must function in the chemically complex atmosphere it helps control.
key_works: OECD NEA and Becker Technologies (2020–2024), [*THAI Experiments on Mitigation measures… (THEMIS)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_58863/thai-experiments-on-mitigation-measures-and-source-term-issues-to-support-analysis-and-further-improvement-of-severe-accident-management-measures-themis-project).

title: Containment stratification under interacting safety systems
open: Predict formation and erosion of light-gas layers in compartmented containments when sprays, coolers, and recombiners operate together. Quantify sensitivity to turbulence, obstructions, wall condensation, and radiation using blind comparisons across geometries.
status: HYMERES-2 experiments concluded in 2021. Paladino et al. (2022) documented extensive PANDA results; reliable transfer to plant geometries remains a stronger unresolved target.
why: Spatial concentration maxima govern mitigation needs that well-mixed models can miss.
key_works: D. Paladino et al. (2022), *PANDA experiments within the OECD/NEA HYMERES-2 project on containment hydrogen distribution, thermal radiation and suppression pool phenomena*, [DOI:10.1016/j.nucengdes.2022.111777](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nucengdes.2022.111777).

title: Organic iodine from aged containment surfaces
open: Predict organic-iodine formation and destruction from aged paints and other surfaces under irradiation, humidity changes, and chemical contamination. Separate surface-layer, pore, and bulk-water reactions sufficiently to transfer kinetics among coatings.
status: BIP phases through 2019 measured adsorption, desorption, and organic-iodide production. Paint aging and confident reactor-scale extrapolation remained explicit programme targets.
why: Organic iodine can be harder to retain than other iodine forms.
key_works: OECD NEA and Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (2007–2019), [*Behaviour of Iodine Project (BIP)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_24819/behaviour-of-iodine-project-bip).

title: Delayed remobilization of deposited fission products
open: Predict when deposited iodine-, caesium-, and molybdenum-bearing material becomes airborne again as temperature, radiation, and atmosphere change. Close species-dependent balances over repeated deposition and remobilization.
status: ESTER completed semi-integral and real-fuel-derived-deposit tests and concluded in March 2025. General reaction-history-dependent predictions remain the open synthesis problem.
why: Late releases can occur after initial transport and cooling conditions change.
key_works: OECD NEA, ASNR, and CEA (2020–2025), [*Experiments on Source Term for Delayed Releases (ESTER) Project*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_58926/experiments-on-source-term-for-delayed-releases-ester-project).

title: Species-resolved aerosol pool scrubbing
open: Predict retention for aerosol sizes and chemical forms as bubbles rise during transients. Couple breakup, hygroscopic growth, dissolution, and re-entrainment, validating beyond an aggregate decontamination factor.
status: THEMIS completed pool-scrubbing experiments and a benchmark by its 2024 closeout; transfer among mixtures, bubble populations, and evolving chemistry remains incomplete.
why: The least-retained fraction can dominate airborne activity.
key_works: OECD NEA and Becker Technologies (2020–2024), [*THAI Experiments on Mitigation measures… (THEMIS)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_58863/thai-experiments-on-mitigation-measures-and-source-term-issues-to-support-analysis-and-further-improvement-of-severe-accident-management-measures-themis-project).

title: Gas-fast-reactor heat removal after depressurization
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate reliable decay-heat removal for a gas-cooled fast reactor after simultaneous pressure loss and loss of normal electrical support, accounting for realistic flow resistance and degraded equipment.
status: A central GFR issue since the 2002 Generation IV roadmap. ALLEGRO analyses and experiments have advanced; Bali and Mayer’s 2025 investigation supplies a recent partial result.
why: Determines whether the fast-spectrum helium concept can satisfy its safety case.
key_works: Stainsby et al. (2009), *Gas Cooled Fast Reactor Research and Development in the European Union*, [DOI:10.1155/2009/238624](https://doi.org/10.1155/2009/238624); Bali and Mayer (2025), [*Investigation of decay heat removal systems in the ALLEGRO helium-cooled fast reactor*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0029549325001293).

title: Integrated supercritical-water reactor qualification
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate a supercritical-water reactor system whose coupled thermal limits, material lifetime, startup behavior, and protection functions remain acceptable over an independently assessed operating envelope.
status: European SCWR research dates to 2000. Schulenberg’s 2025 assessment documents substantial code and concept development; 2026 symposium reporting still identifies prototype-oriented research needs.
why: Tests whether proposed efficiency and plant simplification survive integrated engineering constraints.
key_works: T. Schulenberg (2025), *25 Years of supercritical water-cooled reactor research in Europe: Lessons learned and future challenges*, [DOI:10.1016/j.nucengdes.2025.114317](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nucengdes.2025.114317); W. Ambrosini et al. (2026), [*Highlights from the 11th International Symposium on Supercritical Water-cooled Reactors*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0029549326002505).

title: Lead-coolant freezing detection and recovery
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Detect incipient lead blockage and validate safe recovery after extended cooling or interrupted restart, including local freezing, natural convection, and structural loading. Establish transferable experimental criteria beyond nominal temperature margins.
status: Long recognized in lead-reactor development. The 2024 LEFREEZ programme and 2025 coupled solidification studies provide dedicated experimental and modeling foundations.
why: Prevents manageable shutdowns from causing persistent circulation loss or damage.
key_works: Lee et al. (2024), *Westinghouse Test Facilities for Lead Fast Reactor Development*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2023.2197667](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2023.2197667).

title: Quantitative inspection through hot liquid sodium
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Qualify repeatable defect sizing and component localization through hot, opaque sodium under representative radiation, wetting, geometry, and surface conditions. Report detection probability and false calls for realistic defects.
status: Under-sodium ultrasonic viewing has decades of prototypes and operational precedents; waveguides and arrays have improved access. Transferable quantitative inspection reliability remains the specific gap.
why: Enables maintenance and life extension without unnecessary draining and exposure.
key_works: Griffin et al. (2009), [*Under-Sodium Viewing: A Review of Ultrasonic Imaging Technology for Liquid Metal Fast Reactors*](https://www.pnnl.gov/publications/under-sodium-viewing-review-ultrasonic-imaging-technology-liquid-metal-fast-reactors), PNNL-18292.

title: Whole-circuit liquid-fuel inventory validation
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Validate time-dependent radionuclide inventories throughout a liquid-fuel reactor, including deposits and auxiliary systems, with measured uncertainties and mass-balance closure. Predict where decay heat and radiological inventory reside.
status: SCALE 6.3 introduced liquid-fuel depletion capabilities, reported by Hartanto et al. in 2024. Analytical and application comparisons provide partial evidence; complete physical inventory validation remains difficult.
why: Supports maintenance, waste planning, and source-term assessment.
key_works: Hartanto et al. (2024), [*SCALE depletion capabilities for molten salt reactors and other liquid-fueled systems*](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/scale-depletion-capabilities-molten-salt-reactors-and-other-liquid-fueled-systems).

title: Long-service reliability of salt drainage systems
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate that a liquid-fuel drainage system retains its required function after prolonged irradiation, chemistry changes, cycling, and equipment aging, including common-cause loss of support systems.
status: Freeze valves operated in historical salt experiments; Chisholm et al. reviewed that experience in 2020. Modern systems still require qualification over their complete service lives.
why: Establishes demonstrated reliability for a proposed passive shutdown feature.
key_works: Chisholm et al. (2020), *A unique molten salt reactor feature—The freeze valve system: Design, operating experience, and reliability*, [DOI:10.1016/j.nucengdes.2020.110803](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nucengdes.2020.110803).

title: Cascading heat-pipe failures in microreactors
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Determine experimentally whether heat-pipe losses overload neighboring pipes and cause progressive cooling loss. Validate coupled thermal, structural, and control predictions under degraded interfaces.
status: Single-failure simulations and adaptive-control studies exist. MAGNET’s 2024 report identifies limits in its ability to emulate cascading failures.
why: Establishes actual robustness of distributed passive cooling.
key_works: Oncken, Lin, and Agarwal (2024), *Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Heat Pipe–Cooled Microreactors Under Normal and Heat Pipe Failure Conditions*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2024.2342206](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2024.2342206); T. J. Morton et al. (2024), *Development, Construction, and Operation of the Agile Non-nuclear Microreactor Experimental Test Bed (MAGNET) and Helium Component Test Facility (He-CTF)*, [DOI:10.1080/00295639.2024.2384218](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295639.2024.2384218).

title: Nuclear-coupled supercritical-CO2 cycle endurance
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate integrated supercritical-CO2 conversion with representative nuclear heat interfaces, repeated transients, realistic heat rejection, and verified exchanger integrity. Quantify lifetime efficiency and maintenance cost.
status: Cycle analyses and component tests have advanced substantially since the 2000s. Complete endurance under coupled nuclear service remains a design-specific qualification target.
why: Determines whether compact conversion delivers practical cost and efficiency benefits.
key_works: Qi et al. (2018), *The application of supercritical CO2 in nuclear engineering: A review*, [DOI:10.1177/1757482X18765377](https://doi.org/10.1177/1757482X18765377).

title: Qualified transport for new reactor-fuel forms
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Establish economical, licensed transport capacity for the chemical and physical forms required by advanced reactors, supported by shared validation data and reliable logistics. Measure delivered capacity and turnaround time.
status: DOE supported new TRISO transport experiments and package development in 2025. These programmes address continuing form-specific infrastructure gaps.
why: Reactor and fuel-producer readiness must be connected by qualified transport.
key_works: U.S. DOE (2025), [*National Lab Conducts First-of-a-Kind Experiments to Support Transportation of TRISO Fuels*](https://www.energy.gov/ne/articles/national-lab-conducts-first-kind-experiments-support-transportation-triso-fuels); DOE, [*HALEU Transportation*](https://www.energy.gov/ne/haleu-transportation).

title: Helium turbomachinery lifetime and maintainability
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate high-availability helium power conversion with acceptable leakage, bearing reliability, rotor dynamics, and maintenance under reactor-compatible temperatures and duty cycles.
status: Helium turbines and test facilities have operated; McDonald’s 2012 review records substantial experience. Economical, maintainable reactor integration remains design-specific and incompletely demonstrated.
why: Tests the practical value of gas-cycle nuclear plants.
key_works: C. F. McDonald (2012), *Helium turbomachinery operating experience from gas turbine power plants and test facilities*, [DOI:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2012.02.041](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2012.02.041).

title: Separating radiation drift from real optical-sensor signals
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Distinguish true temperature or strain changes from radiation-induced attenuation, compaction, and coating effects in distributed optical sensors. Validate stable calibration under simultaneous irradiation and thermal cycling.
status: In-pile sensing is demonstrated. Conrad and Woods measured damage and recovery in coated fibers in 2024; mixed-field lifetime correction remains device- and environment-dependent.
why: Enables trustworthy measurements where conventional sensors are sparse or inaccessible.
key_works: Conrad and Woods (2024), *Irradiation damage and recovery in gold-coated fiber optics*, [DOI:10.1016/j.net.2023.11.004](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.net.2023.11.004); INL (2025), [*Advanced Sensors and Instrumentation: FY2024 Summary of Accomplishments*](https://asi.inl.gov/content/uploads/47/2025/06/24-51032_R5_FY24-ASI-Summary-of-Accomplishments.pdf).

title: Online calibration despite common-mode drift
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Detect and correct sensor drift when nominally redundant instruments drift together and operating conditions change. Demonstrate traceable uncertainty without assuming a perfect reference channel.
status: Online calibration monitoring has decades of development; Ramuhalli et al. introduced recalibration algorithms in 2022. Common-mode identifiability and field qualification remain harder than detecting one inconsistent sensor.
why: Reduces intrusive calibration without hiding systematic measurement error.
key_works: Ramuhalli et al. (2022), *A Methodology for Online Sensor Recalibration*, [DOI:10.36001/phmconf.2022.v14i1.3274](https://doi.org/10.36001/phmconf.2022.v14i1.3274).

title: Quantifying digital common-cause failure
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Estimate defensible failure bounds for diverse digital protection channels sharing specifications, tools, suppliers, or development assumptions. Validate whether proposed diversity measures predict actual independence.
status: NRC’s 2010 diversity-strategy report provides architectures and assessment foundations. Credible quantitative probabilities for rare shared software defects remain unresolved.
why: Prevents nominal redundancy from overstating reliability.
key_works: Wood et al. (2010), [*Diversity Strategies for Nuclear Power Plant Instrumentation and Control Systems*](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/diversity-strategies-nuclear-power-plant-instrumentation-and-control-systems-0), NUREG/CR-7007.

title: Assurance for adaptive reactor controllers
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Demonstrate that an adaptive controller maintains a specified safe envelope during model mismatch, sensor faults, and mode changes, with an independently verified fallback. Bound permissible online adaptation.
status: Heat-pipe microreactor adaptive control was demonstrated in simulation in 2024. Full autonomous-operation qualification requires additional assurance.
why: Makes advanced automation assessable as a complete control system.
key_works: Oncken, Lin, and Agarwal (2024), *Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Heat Pipe–Cooled Microreactors Under Normal and Heat Pipe Failure Conditions*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2024.2342206](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2024.2342206).

title: Human performance during simultaneous module upsets
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Establish operator-team workload and recovery reliability when several reactor modules require attention at once. Validate staffing and interfaces with trained teams and correlated off-normal scenarios.
status: NRC identified SMR human-performance issues in 2012, followed by reviewer guidance. Single-unit experience provides incomplete evidence for concurrent multi-module events.
why: Determines whether multi-module operating concepts are credible.
key_works: J. O’Hara, J. Higgins, and M. Pena (2012), [*Human-Performance Issues Related to the Design and Operation of Small Modular Reactors*](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/nuregs/contract/cr7126/), NUREG/CR-7126.

title: Remote operation through communication loss
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Demonstrate safe, recoverable remote reactor operation through communication failures, delayed telemetry, and lost remote support, including unambiguous transfer of responsibility to humans.
status: Stevens et al. proposed and tested a digital-twin framework in 2023; subsequent microreactor programmes provide testbeds. Complete mission-duration reliability remains a deployment target.
why: Supports remote civilian energy despite intermittent connectivity and delayed specialist access.
key_works: Stevens et al. (2023), [*Digital Twin Framework for the Resilient Remote Monitoring and Operation of Nuclear Microreactors*](https://openaccess.cms-conferences.org/publications/book/978-1-958651-93-3/article/978-1-958651-93-3_1).

title: Cybersecurity assurance for evolving digital twins
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Verify that updates to plant digital twins, data pipelines, and learned models preserve security boundaries and safety-relevant behavior. Demonstrate secure recovery and evidence continuity through controlled defensive testing.
status: Yockey, Erickson, and Spirito’s 2023 assessment identifies concerns introduced by machine-learning control. Assurance across continuing updates remains incomplete.
why: Prevents software evolution from invalidating earlier safety and security assessments.
key_works: Yockey, Erickson, and Spirito (2023), [*Cyber threat assessment of machine learning driven autonomous control systems of nuclear power plants*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0149197023003955).

title: Cross-plant fault-diagnosis benchmark data
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Build a permissioned or openly releasable dataset containing synchronized measurements, maintenance outcomes, uncertain fault onset, and plant identifiers for genuine cross-plant evaluation. Include missing data and benign operating changes.
status: Nuclear big-data workshops and prognostics studies identify access and representativeness barriers. Many classifiers are evaluated on simulations or narrow component datasets.
why: Tests whether diagnostics transfer to different plants.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2021), *Prognostics and Health Management in Nuclear Power Plants: An Updated Method-Centric Review With Special Focus on Data-Driven Methods*, [DOI:10.3389/fenrg.2021.696785](https://doi.org/10.3389/fenrg.2021.696785); INL (2024), [*4th Big Data for Nuclear Power Plants Workshop 2023*](https://inl.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/4th-big-data-for-nuclear-power-plants-workshop-2023/).

title: Causal evidence for condition-based maintenance
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Determine whether predictive-maintenance interventions reduce failures, exposure, and total cost after accounting for maintenance-induced changes in observable failures. Use prospective or credible quasi-experimental comparisons.
status: Remaining-life models are well developed in parts of the field. The 2021 PHM review documents deployment gaps; causal benefit remains a stronger target than retrospective prediction.
why: Establishes actual operational benefit.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2021), *Prognostics and Health Management in Nuclear Power Plants*, [DOI:10.3389/fenrg.2021.696785](https://doi.org/10.3389/fenrg.2021.696785).

title: Multi-unit accident risk with shared resources
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Quantify joint accident progression and consequences when units share support systems, staff, access routes, and external hazards. Propagate uncertainty in dependencies instead of summing single-unit risks.
status: Work intensified after 2011. IAEA’s 2023 methodology and site studies provide major partial results; high-consequence dependence and shared-response modeling remain difficult to validate.
why: Produces site-level assessments reflecting correlated events.
key_works: IAEA (2023), [*Multi-unit Probabilistic Safety Assessment*](https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/PUB1820_web.pdf); Coleman et al. (2023), *Assessing the Impact of Common Cause Failures on Site Risk within Level 1 Multi-Unit PSA*, [DOI:10.1155/2023/5889803](https://doi.org/10.1155/2023/5889803).

title: Dispatch that prices nuclear cycling damage
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Jointly optimize electricity dispatch, ancillary services, fuel constraints, and lifetime wear using validated degradation costs. Test the policy against actual operating and maintenance records.
status: Load following is established; Jenkins et al. quantified system benefits in 2018. Credible plant-specific lifetime costs and transfer across operating regimes remain incomplete inputs.
why: Determines when flexibility improves total system value.
key_works: Jenkins et al. (2018), [*The benefits of nuclear flexibility in power system operations with renewable energy*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306261918303180).

title: Nuclear thermal-storage lifetime demonstration
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate storage-coupled nuclear energy that repeatedly separates reactor heat production from electricity demand while meeting efficiency, availability, and lifetime-cost targets. Include actual storage degradation and balance-of-plant costs.
status: Heat-storage concepts and detailed configurations are well developed. Forsberg’s 2022 study analyzes reactor–power-block separation; full lifecycle performance for proposed large systems remains an engineering target.
why: Allows steady reactor operation with dispatchable heat and power.
key_works: C. Forsberg (2022), *Separating Nuclear Reactors from the Power Block with Heat Storage to Improve Economics with Dispatchable Heat and Electricity*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2021.1947121](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2021.1947121).

title: Durable flexible nuclear hydrogen production
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate coupled nuclear heat, electricity, and electrolysis under changing grid and hydrogen demand, including stack degradation, steam-interface transients, product purity, and full delivered cost.
status: DOE-supported nuclear electrolysis demonstrations exist, and INL supports low- and high-temperature pathways. Economical long-duration integrated operation remains the target.
why: Connects nuclear energy to industrial feedstocks and flexible demand.
key_works: INL, [*Hydrogen*](https://inl.gov/integrated-energy/hydrogen/), programme accessed 2026; Westinghouse and INL (2025), [*First-of-a-kind simulator created by Westinghouse and Idaho National Laboratory will improve versatility, profitability of nuclear reactors*](https://info.westinghousenuclear.com/news/first-of-a-kind-simulator-created-by-westinghouse-and-idaho-national-laboratory-will-improve-versatility-profitability-of-nuclear-reactors).

title: Industrial endurance of iodine–sulfur hydrogen cycles
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate sustained closed-loop thermochemical hydrogen production using industrial materials with acceptable corrosion, leakage, separation energy, and replacement rates. Integrate the process with a realistic nuclear heat interface.
status: Continuous laboratory production and industrial-material pilot work have been achieved. JAEA’s 2020 study improved equipment reliability; commercial endurance and economics remain unresolved.
why: Tests hydrogen production driven largely by high-temperature heat.
key_works: Kamiji et al. (2020), [*Reliability improvements of corrosion-resistant equipment for thermochemical water splitting hydrogen production iodine-sulfur process*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0029549320300686).

title: Flexible nuclear desalination with verified isolation
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate economical, flexible water and power co-production with validated isolation, product-water monitoring, and transient response under site-specific demand and seawater conditions.
status: Nuclear desalination has operating precedents and decades of IAEA coordination. New coupled configurations still require transferable cost and safety evidence.
why: Supports reliable water supply where energy and freshwater constraints coincide.
key_works: IAEA (2001), [*Safety aspects of nuclear plants coupled with seawater desalination units*](https://pub.iaea.org/MTCD/publications/PDF/te_1235_prn.pdf), TECDOC-1235; I. Khamis and R. S. El-Emam (2016), *IAEA coordinated research activity on nuclear desalination: the quest for new technologies and techno-economic assessment*, [DOI:10.1016/j.desal.2016.04.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.desal.2016.04.015).

title: Seasonal economics of nuclear district heating
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Determine which combinations of distance, network temperature, storage, building retrofits, and seasonal demand make new nuclear district heat competitive. Validate delivered cost and winter reliability in operating networks.
status: Nuclear district heating already operates; China’s Shidao Bay HTGR supplied district heat in 2024. Replicability across urban forms and financing settings remains unresolved.
why: Extends decarbonization to building heat while accounting for distribution infrastructure.
key_works: China Nuclear Energy Association (2024), [*Milestone Achieved: Fourth-Generation Nuclear System Powers Urban District Heating for the First Time*](https://www.china-nea.cn/site/content/45323.html).

title: Safe industrial-heat interfaces across plant boundaries
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Qualify interfaces isolating nuclear heat sources from industrial chemical hazards while tolerating rapid demand changes. Demonstrate that process-plant upsets preserve reactor protection assumptions.
status: HTTR experience and JAEA’s 2020 cogeneration work establish design and licensing foundations. Broader industrial integration requires application-specific validation and commercial demonstration.
why: Enables nuclear steam and high-temperature heat for manufacturing.
key_works: Sato, Aoki, Ohashi, and Yan (2020), [*Research and development for safety and licensing of HTGR cogeneration system*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0029549319305242).

title: Nuclear-supported grid restoration and island operation
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate a nuclear-centered energy island surviving major grid disturbance and supporting staged restoration, with independently established auxiliary-power and control requirements.
status: Island operation has precedents. Greene’s 2018–2019 work defines resilient-plant and black-start functions; prolonged-outage demonstrations across varied restoration conditions remain a systems target.
why: Makes nuclear capacity useful during infrastructure recovery.
key_works: S. R. Greene (2019), *Enhancing Electric Grid, Critical Infrastructure, and Societal Resilience with Resilient Nuclear Power Plants*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2018.1505357](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2018.1505357).

title: Correlated climate-driven nuclear derating
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Predict joint nuclear availability during compound heat, drought, flood, wildfire, and grid events using evolving climate distributions and site-specific cooling constraints. Validate extreme-event dependence.
status: Climate–water generation modeling has advanced since at least the 2010s. Van Vliet et al. quantified vulnerabilities and adaptations in 2016; rare compound events remain uncertain.
why: Prevents overestimation of firm capacity during regional stress.
key_works: M. T. H. van Vliet, D. Wiberg, S. Leduc, and K. Riahi (2016), *Power-generation system vulnerability and adaptation to changes in climate and water resources*, [DOI:10.1038/nclimate2903](https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate2903).

title: Tenfold lower consumptive cooling water
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate tenfold lower annual consumptive cooling water per net megawatt-hour, with no more than 5% annual output loss and 10% total levelized generation-cost premium against a wet-cooled reference under the same climate and duty cycle. These are proposed combined targets.
status: Dry and hybrid cooling reduce water demand with cost and efficiency penalties. Existing adaptation studies establish the trade-off, not this combined performance target.
why: Broadens siting options and reduces drought competition for water.
key_works: Van Vliet et al. (2016), *Power-generation system vulnerability and adaptation to changes in climate and water resources*, [DOI:10.1038/nclimate2903](https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate2903); IAEA (2024), [*Climate Change and Nuclear Power 2024*](https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/PUB9048_web.pdf).

title: Causal decomposition of nuclear cost escalation
open: Identify causal contributions of design complexity, labor productivity, regulation, supply-chain disruption, and financing to cost growth. Separate these from project selection and country effects, then validate predictions on subsequent projects.
status: Debated since the 1960s. Eash-Gates et al.’s 2020 decomposition offers a major explanation for U.S. experience; transferable causal estimates remain contested.
why: Directs cost-reduction efforts toward demonstrated mechanisms.
key_works: Eash-Gates et al. (2020), *Sources of Cost Overrun in Nuclear Power Plant Construction Call for a New Approach to Engineering Design*, [DOI:10.1016/j.joule.2020.10.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2020.10.001).

title: The factory learning–scale trade-off
open: Determine production volumes, design stability, utilization, and module sizes at which repeat manufacturing outweighs lost plant economies of scale. Verify using actual factory and site costs.
status: Decades of SMR modeling establish possible mechanisms. Mignacca and Locatelli’s 2020 review identifies evidence and financing gaps; design-specific manufacturing studies provide partial results.
why: Tests a central economic claim for modular reactors.
key_works: B. Mignacca and G. Locatelli (2020), *Economics and finance of Small Modular Reactors: A systematic review and research agenda*, [DOI:10.1016/j.rser.2019.109519](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2019.109519).

title: Tenfold faster material qualification
open: Reduce qualification time for a specified nuclear material or manufacturing route by at least tenfold while retaining independently demonstrated lifetime prediction and defect-detection reliability. Define an explicit conventional baseline.
status: Accelerated qualification is an active NRC and DOE research direction; 2024–2025 activities address combining evidence. The tenfold target is proposed, without a universally established method.
why: Shortens the interval between promising materials and usable hardware.
key_works: NRC (2024–2025), [*Advanced Manufacturing Technologies*](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/power/amts); Argonne (2023), [*Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies: 2022 Roadmap*](https://nric.inl.gov/content/uploads/34/2024/12/ANL-23-12-Advanced-Materials-and-Manufacturing-Technologies-AMMT-2022-Roadmap.pdf).

title: Qualification transfer between manufacturing machines
open: Determine what evidence preserves qualification when an additively manufactured or powder-metallurgy component’s machine, powder lot, geometry, or process monitoring changes. Bound undetected defects and service-property variation.
status: NRC’s 2023 workshop and DOE’s roadmap address process-specific qualification. Transfer across production conditions remains distinct from qualification of individual specimens or machines.
why: Makes advanced manufacturing scalable.
key_works: NRC (2023), [*Workshop on Advanced Manufacturing Technologies for Nuclear Applications*](https://www.nrc.gov/public-meetings-hearings/conferences-symposia/workshop-on-advanced-manufacturing-technologies-amts-for-nuclear-applications/2023-workshop-on-advanced-manufacturing-technologies-amts-for-nuclear-applications).

title: Tenfold reduction in construction rework
open: Demonstrate an order-of-magnitude reduction in rework hours for a defined construction package using complete design, constructability checks, verified interfaces, and field feedback. Include additional engineering and displaced costs.
status: Rework and declining productivity are documented contributors; Eash-Gates et al. (2020) identify design-related opportunities. The tenfold integrated target is proposed.
why: Reduces schedule and labor costs.
key_works: Eash-Gates et al. (2020), *Sources of Cost Overrun in Nuclear Power Plant Construction Call for a New Approach to Engineering Design*, [DOI:10.1016/j.joule.2020.10.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2020.10.001).

title: Interchangeable qualified nuclear modules
open: Establish interfaces, tolerances, provenance, and acceptance tests permitting modules from different qualified suppliers to be integrated without repeating the entire design and assurance effort.
status: Modular construction exists in selected plants. The National Academies’ 2023 assessment documents continuing supply-chain and execution barriers; broad supplier interchangeability remains a proposed target.
why: Expands competition and reduces dependence on single fabrication paths.
key_works: National Academies (2023), *Laying the Foundation for New and Advanced Nuclear Reactors in the United States*, [DOI:10.17226/26630](https://doi.org/10.17226/26630).

title: Construction-risk contracts that actually reduce total cost
open: Design and evaluate contracts allocating construction risk to parties able to manage it while controlling incentives for delay, hidden changes, and public loss. Compare all-in delivered cost and realized risk.
status: Fixed-price, regulated, and state-backed arrangements exist. DOE’s 2024 Liftoff report identifies financing and risk-management barriers; a generally superior mechanism remains unestablished.
why: Financing can block credible projects or transfer losses without reducing them.
key_works: U.S. DOE (2024), [*Pathways to Commercial Liftoff: Advanced Nuclear*](https://gain.inl.gov/content/uploads/4/2024/11/DOE-Advanced-Nuclear-Liftoff-Report.pdf).

title: Coordinating reactor, fuel, and factory commitments
open: Establish credible commitments synchronizing reactor orders, qualified fuel, factories, and skilled labor without excessive stranded capacity. Test resilience to delayed or canceled orders.
status: DOE’s 2024 Liftoff analysis and SMR finance literature describe mutually dependent investments. Announcements alone do not establish a self-sustaining production system.
why: Resolves coordination failures blocking commercial scale-up.
key_works: U.S. DOE (2024), [*Pathways to Commercial Liftoff: Advanced Nuclear*](https://gain.inl.gov/content/uploads/4/2024/11/DOE-Advanced-Nuclear-Liftoff-Report.pdf); Mignacca and Locatelli (2020), *Economics and finance of Small Modular Reactors*, [DOI:10.1016/j.rser.2019.109519](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2019.109519).

title: Auditable international all-in project costs
open: Create a project-level dataset reconciling overnight costs, financing, cancellations, scope changes, subsidies, construction dates, and accounting definitions. Include unsuccessful projects and trace each value to evidence.
status: Lovering et al.’s 2016 compilation expanded coverage; published replies exposed consequential comparability disputes. A continuously maintained, fully reconciled all-in dataset remains incomplete.
why: Enables credible forecasts and cross-country policy evaluation.
key_works: J. R. Lovering, A. Yip, and T. Nordhaus (2016), *Historical construction costs of global nuclear power reactors*, [DOI:10.1016/j.enpol.2016.01.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2016.01.011); J. Koomey, N. E. Hultman, and A. Grubler (2017), *A reply to “Historical construction costs of global nuclear power reactors”*, [DOI:10.1016/j.enpol.2016.03.052](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2016.03.052).

title: Robust nuclear deployment under competing technology uncertainty
open: Determine deployment strategies remaining valuable across uncertain storage, transmission, demand flexibility, fuel prices, construction delays, and climate constraints. Include option value and irreversible investment.
status: Sepulveda et al. studied nearly 1,000 system cases in 2018, establishing conditional value for firm resources. Robust near-term decisions remain sensitive to costs and system assumptions.
why: Connects research and procurement to realistic system alternatives.
key_works: N. Sepulveda, J. Jenkins, F. de Sisternes, and R. Lester (2018), *The Role of Firm Low-Carbon Electricity Resources in Deep Decarbonization of Power Generation*, [DOI:10.1016/j.joule.2018.08.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2018.08.006).

title: Long-duration fission power on planetary surfaces
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Demonstrate deployable surface-fission power with years of unattended generation, robust heat rejection, startup after transport, and predictable degradation in lunar or Martian environments.
status: KRUSTY’s 2018 ground test established important system behavior; NASA continues development. Multiyear extraterrestrial operation remains undemonstrated by that ground-test evidence.
why: Enables exploration where sunlight and storage are limiting.
key_works: NASA (2021; updated 2026), [*Fission Surface Power*](https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/stmd/fission-surface-power/); NASA (2019), [*The Kilopower Space Nuclear Fission Power Reactor*](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20190026448).

title: Civil floating-reactor lifecycle qualification
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Establish complete safety and responsibility arrangements spanning construction, towing, mooring, operation, extreme marine conditions, relocation, and end-of-life handling for civilian floating reactors.
status: Floating nuclear generation already operates. IAEA’s 2025 INPRO forum and SMR programme identify gaps where nuclear, maritime, transport, and national responsibilities meet.
why: Makes coastal and remote deployment repeatable and governable.
key_works: IAEA (2025), [*24th INPRO Dialogue Forum on the Sustainable Deployment of Floating Nuclear Power Plants*](https://nucleus.iaea.org/sites/INPRO/Pages/df-24.aspx); IAEA (2025), [*SMR Platform Annual Report*](https://nucleus.iaea.org/sites/smr/Shared%20Documents/IAEA%20SMR%20Platform%20Annual%20Report%202025.pdf).

title: Research-reactor conversion without losing scientific capability
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Complete qualification, industrial fabrication, and reactor-specific validation of lower-enrichment fuels for remaining high-performance research reactors while retaining essential irradiation and neutron-beam capabilities.
status: Conversion programmes date to 1978 and have many successes. EU-CONVERSION’s 2024–2028 programme addresses remaining irradiation and supply-chain requirements.
why: Sustains research and isotope production while reducing reliance on highly enriched fuel.
key_works: EU-CONVERSION consortium (2024–2028), [*Supplying the European Research Reactors with Safe Low-Enriched Uranium Fuels for Their Conversion and Long-Term Operation*](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101163752/reporting).

title: Sustainable payment for medical-isotope reserve capacity
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Implement payment and coordination arrangements funding irradiation capacity, outages, reserves, and replacement facilities while preserving patient access to short-lived medical isotopes.
status: The 2009–2010 shortages prompted NEA coordination. Full-cost-recovery methods were published in 2012 and subsequently reviewed; durable supply-chain implementation remains an institutional problem.
why: Prevents shortages of products that cannot be stockpiled like ordinary goods.
key_works: OECD/NEA (2012), [*Full-cost Recovery for Molybdenum-99 Irradiation Services: Methodology and Implementation*](https://www.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_36047/full-cost-recovery-for-molybdenum-99-irradiation-services-methodology-and-implementation?details=true); National Academies (2018), [*Opportunities and Approaches for Supplying Molybdenum-99 and Associated Medical Isotopes to Global Markets*](https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/24909).

title: Accelerator availability for subcritical power systems
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Demonstrate an accelerator-driven civilian system whose beam interruptions, recovery, target lifetime, and thermal cycling permit sustained useful operation. Verify integrated availability over a representative campaign.
status: Pursued for decades. MYRRHA’s staged accelerator work emphasizes reliability, and EU programmes have compared requirements with operating evidence; complete availability demonstration remains open.
why: Determines whether transmutation and irradiation benefits survive interruptions and maintenance.
key_works: SCK CEN, [*MYRRHA linear accelerator*](https://www.myrrha.be/about-myrrha/myrrha-linear-accelerator); EU MAX consortium (2011–2014), [*MYRRHA Accelerator eXperiment*](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/269565/reporting).

title: Radiation-durable recycling solvents over repeated service
open: Demonstrate recycling solvents whose chemical performance survives repeated irradiation, cleaning, and reuse, including accumulated degradation products. Predict service life across representative radiation fields.
status: Mincher et al. (2009) documented radical-driven degradation mechanisms. Established solvents operate, but validated durability of newer systems and their reaction products remains incomplete.
why: Reduces contaminated solvent waste, downtime, and replacement cost.
key_works: B. J. Mincher, G. Elias, L. R. Martin, and S. P. Mezyk (2009), *Radiation chemistry and the nuclear fuel cycle*, [DOI:10.1007/s10967-009-0156-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10967-009-0156-x).

title: Predictive third-phase formation boundaries
open: Predict when recycling solvents separate into an unwanted additional liquid phase, accounting for water, degradation products, and mixed solutes. Validate unseen compositions and identify observable precursors.
status: A longstanding extraction problem. Guerinoni et al. (2026) resolved multiscale structures preceding separation in a model system; reliable prediction for evolving mixtures remains open.
why: Unexpected separation disrupts performance and complicates operation.
key_works: E. Guerinoni et al. (2026), *Pretransitional Multiscale Structure Preceding Third-Phase Formation in Solvent Extraction Systems*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.langmuir.5c05633](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.langmuir.5c05633).

title: Iodine-129 capture followed by durable retention
open: Demonstrate integrated capture of inorganic and organic iodine from variable off-gas, followed by retention through conditioning, storage, and disposal-relevant aging. Include sorbent degradation and secondary releases in material balances.
status: Silver sorbents achieve laboratory capture. Greaney et al. (2023) examined speciation, humidity, gas chemistry, and aging; complete long-term retention remains a separate demonstration.
why: Iodine-129 mobility makes losses across successive handling steps consequential.
key_works: A. T. Greaney et al. (2023), *Abatement of radioiodine in aqueous reprocessing off-gas*, [DOI:10.3389/fchem.2022.1078668](https://doi.org/10.3389/fchem.2022.1078668).

title: Durable krypton capture from dilute radioactive off-gas
open: Demonstrate economical krypton capture from realistic dilute mixed off-gas over repeated cycles under radiation, moisture, and competing gases. Compare energy, replacement materials, and secondary waste with a defined baseline.
status: Trace adsorption is demonstrated, including self-adjusting frameworks in 2022 and radiation-tolerant sorbents in 2024. Long-duration performance and lifetime economics remain qualification targets.
why: Reduces energy and equipment burdens of noble-gas management.
key_works: P. K. Thallapally et al. (2022), *Self-Adjusting Metal-Organic Framework for Efficient Capture of Trace Xenon and Krypton*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202117807](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202117807); A. J. Robinson et al. (2024), *Noble Gas Management with Radiation-Tolerant MOF for Molten Salt Reactors*, [DOI:10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101829](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101829).

title: Integrated conditioning of electrochemical-recycling salt wastes
open: Demonstrate complete routes from representative spent recycling salts to accepted disposal packages, accounting for volatile, liquid, and solid secondary wastes. Optimize total conditioned volume and durability together.
status: Electrochemical treatment and candidate salt waste forms have substantial precedent. Riley’s 2020 comparison identifies further treatment benefits; integrated qualification across variable real wastes remains incomplete.
why: Added treatment residues can erase apparent primary-waste reductions.
key_works: B. J. Riley (2020), *Electrochemical Salt Wasteform Development: A Review of Salt Treatment and Immobilization Options*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.iecr.0c01357](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.0c01357).

title: Complete qualification of a thorium recycle-fuel chain
open: Qualify a specified thorium recycle-fuel option across irradiation, recovery, refabrication, and waste management, including accumulated radioactive daughters. Demonstrate repeatable quality and service behavior over multiple cycles.
status: Thorium fuels have historical irradiation experience. NEA’s 2015 assessment identifies remaining infrastructure and qualification requirements for broader deployment.
why: Establishes whether resource benefits survive real fuel-cycle constraints.
key_works: OECD NEA (2015), *Introduction of Thorium in the Nuclear Fuel Cycle: Short- to long-term considerations*, [DOI:10.1787/9789264241732-en](https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264241732-en).

title: Impurity accumulation through repeated fuel recycling
open: Determine how retained fission products and process-derived impurities accumulate over successive campaigns. Validate effects on fabricated fuel quality and irradiation performance, establishing experimentally supported acceptance criteria.
status: Bays et al. (2009) modeled multirecycle evolution and constraints. Integrated fabrication-and-irradiation evidence remains limited for many proposed fuel options.
why: Small carryover fractions can matter after repeated reuse.
key_works: S. Bays et al. (2009), *Transmutation Dynamics: Impacts of Multi-Recycling on Fuel Cycle Performances*, [INL/EXT-09-16857](https://inldigitallibrary.inl.gov/sites/sti/sti/4336187.pdf).

title: Net repository benefit of transmutation with realistic losses
open: Determine whether specified partitioning-and-transmutation programmes reduce repository footprint and release consequences after processing losses, rejects, secondary wastes, outages, and incomplete deployment. Validate material-flow assumptions and identify benefiting disposal settings.
status: Decades of studies show conditional actinide-inventory and heat reductions. Salvatores and Palmiotti (2011) explain why these need not yield comparably large reductions in repository consequences.
why: Establishes whole-disposal-system benefits.
key_works: M. Salvatores and G. Palmiotti (2011), *Radioactive waste partitioning and transmutation within advanced fuel cycles: Achievements and challenges*, [DOI:10.1016/j.ppnp.2010.10.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ppnp.2010.10.001).

title: High-burnup cladding after decades of thermal history
open: Predict residual ductility and fracture resistance after realistic drying, cooling, and storage histories. Validate blind predictions across cladding alloys against aged irradiated material.
status: NWTRB’s 2021 review identified representativeness and integration gaps. Short specimens and accelerated histories provide incomplete long-term validation.
why: Supports justified storage extensions and later handling.
key_works: NWTRB (2021), [*Evaluation of the Department of Energy’s Research Program to Examine the Performance of Commercial High Burnup Spent Nuclear Fuel During Extended Storage and Transportation*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/our-work/reports/evaluation-of-the-department-of-energy's-research-program-to-examine-the-performance-of-commercial-high-burnup-spent-nuclear-fuel-during-extended-storage-and-transportation-(july-2021)).

title: Transport mechanics of genuinely aged fuel assemblies
open: Establish assembly-level failure bounds for vibration and handling after extended storage, including interactions among rods, pellets, spacers, and supports. Validate with representative irradiated assemblies.
status: Transport experience supports existing practice. NWTRB’s 2021 assessment identifies additional evidence needed for high-burnup, extended-storage combinations.
why: Supports containment while avoiding unnecessary repackaging.
key_works: NWTRB (2021), [*Evaluation of the Department of Energy’s Research Program to Examine the Performance of Commercial High Burnup Spent Nuclear Fuel During Extended Storage and Transportation*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/our-work/reports/evaluation-of-the-department-of-energy's-research-program-to-examine-the-performance-of-commercial-high-burnup-spent-nuclear-fuel-during-extended-storage-and-transportation-(july-2021)).

title: Site-specific canister corrosion forecasting
open: Forecast chloride deposition, wetting, pit initiation, and crack-growth distributions from site weather and measured canister surfaces. Demonstrate calibrated remaining-life predictions across coastal and inland installations.
status: Laboratory mechanisms and deposition models exist. Suffield et al.’s 2023 report, posted in 2024, developed heated-canister deposition modeling while describing coastal field demonstration as prospective.
why: Enables evidence-based inspection intervals and targeted maintenance.
key_works: S. R. Suffield et al. (2023), [*Thermal and Deposition Modeling Update for the Canister Deposition Field Demonstration*](https://www.pnnl.gov/publications/thermal-and-deposition-modeling-update-canister-deposition-field-demonstration), PNNL-34772.

title: Qualified inspection through restricted canister access
open: Demonstrate repeatable defect detection and sizing across accessible loaded-canister regions, with quantified coverage and false-negative probability. Represent service heat, radiation, geometry, surfaces, and sensor aging.
status: Meyer et al. reported multiple NDE demonstrations in 2021. Restricted access and harsh environments remain central qualification constraints.
why: Makes aging-management claims directly testable.
key_works: R. M. Meyer et al. (2021), *Inservice Inspection of Extended Dry Storage of Spent Nuclear Fuel, Part II: NDE/Sensor Technology Development and Codification*, [DOI:10.1115/PVP2021-62069](https://doi.org/10.1115/PVP2021-62069).

title: Storage-to-transport eligibility of existing canister contents
open: Produce an auditable inventory of already-loaded canisters’ transport eligibility, missing evidence, and required interventions. Resolve incompatibilities between storage contents and transport approvals.
status: NWTRB identified this implementation gap in 2024, requesting comprehensive treatment of contents not then approved for transport.
why: Prevents stranded fuel and unexpected handling programmes.
key_works: NWTRB (2024), [*Evaluation of the U.S. Department of Energy Research and Development Activities on the Disposition of Commercial Spent Nuclear Fuel in Dual-Purpose Canisters*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/docs/default-source/reports/nwtrb_feb2024_report_evaluation_csnf_dpcs.pdf).

title: Direct disposal of large dual-purpose canisters
open: Establish which existing canisters suit a specified repository, accounting jointly for heat, degradation, emplacement, and postclosure safety. Compare direct disposal against repackaging on total burden.
status: DOE has modeling programmes; NWTRB’s 2024 review requested stronger integrated comparison and postclosure analysis.
why: Could avoid extensive additional fuel handling and waste.
key_works: NWTRB (2024), [*Evaluation of the U.S. Department of Energy Research and Development Activities on the Disposition of Commercial Spent Nuclear Fuel in Dual-Purpose Canisters*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/docs/default-source/reports/nwtrb_feb2024_report_evaluation_csnf_dpcs.pdf).

title: Thermodynamic data beyond dilute equilibrium solutions
open: Supply consistent thermodynamic data, uncertainties, and validity ranges for radionuclides in hot, saline, organic-bearing repository waters and solid solutions. Validate mixed-system predictions, including kinetic limitations.
status: NEA-TDB and national databases provide foundations. EURAD-2’s DITUSC gap study ended in September 2026 and identified THERMOGAP as follow-up.
why: Reduces unsupported extrapolation in release assessments.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Development and Improvement of Thermodynamic Understanding for Use in Nuclear Waste Disposal Safety Case*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/development-and-improvement-thermodynamic-understanding-use-nuclear-waste-disposal).

title: Valid acceleration of waste-glass durability tests
open: Determine which accelerated conditions preserve mechanisms governing long-term glass release. Establish transfer rules and uncertainty bounds connecting tests, natural analogues, and repository conditions for specified glass families.
status: Standard methods date to the 1980s. Thorpe et al. (2021) document methodological progress and composition-dependent responses; a universal acceleration factor remains unjustified.
why: Accelerates qualification while preserving relevant chemistry.
key_works: C. L. Thorpe et al. (2021), *Forty Years of Durability Assessment of Nuclear Waste Glass by Standard Methods*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4).

title: Waste-glass alteration-resumption boundaries
open: Predict whether, when, and how strongly secondary-mineral precipitation restarts glass alteration under evolving repository chemistry. Distinguish persistently passivated compositions and environments from those entering faster corrosion regimes.
status: Recognized for decades. Fournier et al. (2017) linked seeded zeolite precipitation to rate changes and strong temperature and pH dependence; transfer across complex glasses remains incomplete.
why: Resolves a consequential long-term release uncertainty.
key_works: M. Fournier et al. (2017), *Contribution of Zeolite-Seeded Experiments to the Understanding of Resumption of Glass Alteration*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-017-0018-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-017-0018-x).
aliases: Stage-three glass corrosion; resumption of alteration.

title: Passivating-gel maturation mechanisms
open: Derive predictive relations among alteration-layer structure, water and solute transport, and declining glass-dissolution rate. Distinguish mechanisms through tracer measurements and predict unseen aging trajectories.
status: Narayanasamy et al. (2025) compared gels aged seven days to 27 years, establishing changing transport behavior while retaining uncertainty about passivation and late-time rate limitation.
why: Replaces empirical long-term fits with transferable release models.
key_works: S. Narayanasamy et al. (2025), *Insights into Gel Maturation from Alteration of Borosilicate Glass from 7 Days to 27 Years*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-025-00664-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-025-00664-w).

title: Centuries-scale durability of alternative cementitious waste forms
open: Qualify geopolymer and magnesian-cement forms for specified wastes under realistic leaching, radiation, mechanical, and chemical histories. Determine when matrix degradation changes radionuclide release.
status: Short-term demonstrations include PREDIS work. EURAD-2 L’OPERA’s March 2026 update reports protocols and initial experiments; long-term performance remains an explicit objective.
why: Expands disposal-compatible options for difficult wastes.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Long-Term Performance of Waste Matrices (L’OPERA)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/long-term-performance-waste-matrices-lopera).

title: Reactivation of aluminium corrosion inside waste packages
open: Predict and prevent renewed corrosion of aluminium-bearing waste after initially protective immobilization environments evolve. Validate gas generation, swelling, and release under later repository chemistry.
status: Binders can suppress early corrosion. Fernández-García and Alonso (2025) demonstrated reactivation in phosphate and Portland-based forms under simulated alkaline repository conditions.
why: Avoids late gas-generation and package-deformation surprises.
key_works: C. Fernández-García and M. C. Alonso (2025), *Aluminium Corrosion Reactivation in MKPC and Portland-Based Waste Forms under Simulated Alkaline Repository Conditions*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.156064](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.156064).

title: Disposal-qualified conditioning of difficult organic wastes
open: Demonstrate scalable conditioning for specified resins, oils, and organic liquids, accounting for secondary residues, gas evolution, and acceptance criteria. Close waste balances and validate packages across feed variability.
status: EURAD, THERAMIN, and PREDIS established candidates. STREAM’s 2025–2026 updates report selection milestones while identifying scale-up, compatibility, and secondary-waste gaps.
why: Closes management routes for difficult operational and decommissioning inventories.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Sustainable Treatment and Immobilisation of Challenging Waste (STREAM)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/sustainable-treatment-and-immobilisation-challenging-waste-stream).

title: Carbon-14 speciation and release from irradiated graphite
open: Predict releasable carbon-14 fractions and dissolved, gaseous, organic, and inorganic forms across graphite manufacturing and irradiation histories. Validate laboratory-to-disposal transport relationships.
status: CARBOWASTE and CAST substantially improved inventories and measurements; CAST’s final symposium was in 2018. Heterogeneity and release chemistry remain assessment uncertainties.
why: Chemical form can govern mobility more strongly than total activity.
key_works: CAST consortium (2018), [*Final Overview of CAST*](https://igdtp.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/CAST-2018-D-7.23-Final-Overview-of-CAST_version-2.pdf), D7.23; [CAST project](https://www.projectcast.eu/).

title: Repository performance of spent TRISO fuel
open: Establish radionuclide-release models for irradiated TRISO particles and surrounding graphite after long aging and barrier degradation. Compare intact, imperfect, and damaged populations using representative samples.
status: Reactor-temperature retention is well studied. Gadey et al. (2024) map management options; repository performance remains sensitive to waste-form assumptions.
why: Evaluates advanced-reactor waste claims on actual final forms.
key_works: H. Gadey et al. (2024), *Options for Managing Spent TRi-structural ISOtropic Nuclear Fuel*, [arXiv:2403.18849](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.18849).

title: Representative spent-fuel dissolution source terms
open: Quantify radionuclide release as groundwater contact, radiolysis, redox chemistry, and irradiated-fuel microstructure evolve. Establish interlaboratory reproducibility and identify conservative assumptions that can be refined.
status: FIRST-Nuclides and DisCo supplied substantial evidence. SAREC’s March 2026 update reports active experiments and an initial dissolution database; broader fuel coverage remains unfinished.
why: Improves the connection between fuel properties and repository safety.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Release of Safety Relevant Radionuclides from Spent Nuclear Fuel under Deep Disposal Conditions (SAREC)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/release-safety-relevant-radionuclides-spent-nuclear-fuel-under-deep-disposal).

title: Heterogeneous bentonite self-sealing at full scale
open: Predict whether construction heterogeneity, friction, gaps, and groundwater chemistry converge toward adequate long-term sealing. Validate scaling to repository-sized installations and alternative bentonite sources.
status: Laboratory and underground programmes support bentonite use. EURAD-2 ANCHORS, launched in 2024, targets heterogeneity, chemistry, scale, and benchmarking beyond existing models.
why: Supports robust acceptance criteria and alternative supplies.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Hydraulic Mechanical Chemical Evolution of Bentonite for Barriers Optimisation (ANCHORS)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/hydraulic-mechanical-chemical-evolution-bentonite-barriers-optimisation-anchors).

title: Coupled mechanical and corrosion failure of disposal containers
open: Establish container-lifetime bounds when corrosion, residual stress, creep, and barrier evolution interact. Test whether separate degradation allowances remain conservative for particular materials.
status: Individual processes have decades of evidence. InCoManD’s 2025–2026 programme addresses joint degradation and field conditions, including coatings and alternative materials.
why: Prevents independent component assumptions from overstating combined durability.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Innovative and New Container/Canister Materials under Disposal Fields Conditions: Manufacturing Feasibility and Improved Durability*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/innovative-and-new-containercanister-materials-under-disposal-fields-conditions).

title: Dilatant gas migration through clay barriers
open: Predict gas breakthrough, pathway creation, resealing, and coupled water movement under realistic clay-barrier stress histories. Reproduce independent laboratory and large-scale experiments without retuning mechanisms for each test.
status: DECOVALEX-2019 compared modeling approaches; DECOVALEX-2023 Task B extended work toward larger experiments. Gas-pathway transferability remains unresolved.
why: Constrains pressure and transport effects of repository-generated gases.
key_works: DECOVALEX (2019–2023), [*DECOVALEX-2023 Task B: Gas Transport in Clay*](https://decovalex.org/past-phases/D-2023/task-b).

title: Microbial activity across repository transitions
open: Predict microbial activity as compacted barriers change temperature, saturation, nutrients, and redox state. Link activity to consequential sulfide and gas production using direct metabolic evidence.
status: Sidhu et al.’s 2025 MaCoTe results found little change in inner-bentonite microbial abundance over seven years. Broader transitions, interfaces, and supply conditions remain untested.
why: Establishes when microbial processes matter to corrosion and transport.
key_works: H. S. Sidhu et al. (2025), *Minimal Changes in Microbial Abundances and Diversity over 7 Years of Emplacement for Modules of Compacted Bentonite Exposed to Natural Groundwater*, [DOI:10.1128/aem.01950-24](https://doi.org/10.1128/aem.01950-24).

title: Colloid-facilitated transport across fracture networks
open: Upscale colloid attachment, detachment, filtration, aggregation, and radionuclide exchange from individual fractures to heterogeneous host rock. Predict transport tails under changing chemistry and flow pathways.
status: Experiments and models establish mechanisms. Ma et al.’s 2024 review identifies persistent mismatch between experimental and safety-assessment scales.
why: Bounds migration pathways poorly represented by dissolved-species models.
key_works: F. Ma et al. (2024), *Incorporating Cross-Scale Insights into Colloid-Facilitated Radionuclide Transport in Fractured Rocks: A Critical Review*, [DOI:10.1016/j.earscirev.2024.104974](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2024.104974).

title: Repository climate and biosphere transitions
open: Construct defensible bounds linking climate, sea level, glaciation, erosion, groundwater, and biosphere pathways over repository timescales. Identify decisions robust across plausible trajectories.
status: Climate scenarios already enter safety cases. EURAD-2 CLIMATE completed gap mapping in September 2026 and identified INSURANCE as follow-up; coupled impacts remain an active agenda.
why: Tests long-term safety assumptions against environmental nonstationarity.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Impact of Climate Change on Nuclear Waste Management (CLIMATE)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/impact-climate-change-nuclear-waste-management-climate).

title: Radionuclide retention under chemical perturbations
open: Predict retention when salinity, pH, redox, organics, or mineral assemblages change, including hysteresis and kinetics. Validate transfer to intact clay, granite, and cementitious disposal cells.
status: Equilibrium sorption has substantial evidence. RAMPEC’s 2024–2026 agenda identifies perturbed systems and cell-scale transport as insufficiently constrained, with experiments and a database prototype underway.
why: Determines when conventional retention parameters remain reliable.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Radionuclide Mobility under Perturbed Conditions (RAMPEC)*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/radionuclide-mobility-under-perturbed-conditions-rampec).

title: Corrosion memory of copper disposal barriers
open: Determine how early moist or unsaturated corrosion changes later copper-container behavior after heating, drying, and resaturation. Quantify effects of prior damage and corrosion products on lifetime estimates.
status: Copper corrosion has decades of study. Harper, Brown, and Amos (2024) identify early unsaturated conditions and compounded corrosion history as understudied for the Canadian concept.
why: Tests whether successive environments can be treated independently.
key_works: C. O. Harper, J. L. Brown, and R. T. Amos (2024), *Corrosion Processes Affecting Copper-Coated Used Fuel Containers for the Disposal of Spent Nuclear Fuel: Critical Review of the State-of-Knowledge*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-024-00540-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-024-00540-z).

title: Useful repository monitoring without compromising isolation
open: Develop monitoring that discriminates consequential departures from expected behavior while preserving barriers and supporting closure decisions. Quantify information value, sensor aging, recoverability, and observational limits.
status: Underground laboratories and national programmes demonstrate methods. NWTRB’s 2018 comparison documents differing approaches; reconciling durable observations with final sealing remains programme-specific.
why: Connects construction evidence, oversight, and passive safety.
key_works: NWTRB (2018), [*Geologic Repositories: Performance Monitoring and Retrievability of Emplaced High-Level Radioactive Waste and Spent Nuclear Fuel*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/our-work/reports/geologic-repositories-performance-monitoring-and-retrievability-of-emplaced-high-level-radioactive-waste-and-spent-nuclear-fuel).

title: Activation inventories with incomplete historical records
open: Reconstruct spatial radionuclide inventories when original trace-element composition and irradiation histories are incomplete. Validate uncertainty against withheld destructive samples, particularly near classification boundaries.
status: Activation calculations are mature; IAEA’s 2019 methodology documents their application. Legacy-input reconstruction and representative sampling remain project-specific limitations.
why: Improves dismantling plans and avoids misclassification of large volumes.
key_works: IAEA (2019), [*Methodologies for Assessing the Induced Activation Source Term for Use in Decommissioning Applications*](https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/P1823_web.pdf), Safety Reports Series 95.

title: Hard-to-measure nuclides in heterogeneous waste packages
open: Quantify difficult-to-measure radionuclides in heterogeneous bulk waste with disposal-relevant uncertainty. Determine when correlations with readily measured nuclides transfer and when direct sampling is indispensable.
status: Scaling factors and radiochemistry provide partial solutions. ICARUS identifies continuing chlorine-36, calcium-41, and technetium-99 needs; its 2026 programme plans comparisons and blind tests.
why: Reduces misclassification and unnecessary conditioning.
key_works: EURAD-2 (2024–2026), [*Innovative Characterisation Techniques for Large Volumes—ICARUS*](https://www.ejp-eurad.eu/implementation/innovative-characterisation-techniques-large-volumes-icarus).

title: Representative concrete-clearance measurements
open: Demonstrate surveys and sampling reliably distinguishing reusable concrete from radioactive waste despite patchy contamination and depth gradients. Validate false-clearance probabilities at practical demolition throughput.
status: Measurements and clearance procedures exist. Jung et al. (2024) developed concrete reference material with beta and gamma emitters; transfer to heterogeneous structures remains incomplete.
why: Supports defensible reuse and smaller disposal volumes.
