key_works: S. Chatterjee et al. (2025), *Influence of temperature, initial grain-boundary bubble density and grain structure on fission gas behaviour in UO₂: a 3D hybrid multiscale study*, [arXiv:2511.20352](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20352).

title: Transient burst fission-gas release
open: Predict rapid gas release during power changes from measured pre-transient microstructure, including grain-face crack opening and healing. Reproduce timing and quantity in withheld transients where ordinary diffusion contributes little.
status: Burst release has long resisted purely diffusional treatments. NEA’s dedicated benchmark isolates short transients to distinguish the mechanism from slower diffusion.
why: Bursts alter internal pressure and fuel–cladding heat transfer during transients.
key_works: OECD NEA, [*Burst Fission Gas Release Benchmark of the Expert Group on Reactor Fuel Performance*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_70791/burst-fission-gas-release-fgr-benchmark-of-the-expert-group-on-reactor-fuel-performance-egrfp).

title: Predicting high-burnup restructuring onset
open: Predict where and when original UO₂ grains subdivide, distinguishing polygonization, recrystallization, and bubble-assisted subdivision. Predict boundary misorientation and restructured volume across irradiation histories without imposing a universal burnup threshold.
status: Studied since the original rim-effect observations. Gerczak et al. demonstrated polygonization in a particular irradiated pellet in 2018; general onset and history dependence remain unresolved.
why: Restructuring changes gas storage, conductivity, and susceptibility to fine fragmentation.
key_works: T. J. Gerczak et al. (2018), *Restructuring in high burnup UO₂ studied using modern electron microscopy*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2018.05.077](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2018.05.077).

title: Microstructure-specific fuel pulverization thresholds
open: Establish which combinations of bubble pressure, grain subdivision, cracks, and transient heating produce fine fragments during loss of coolant. Predict fragment-size distributions in previously unseen irradiated material.
status: The 2021 assessment identified substantial gaps. McKinney et al. (2026) associate fragmentation with high bubble and grain-boundary densities and observe central dark-zone fragmentation; transferable thresholds remain unvalidated.
why: Fine fragmentation can change fuel location and accident heat-removal requirements.
key_works: N. Capps et al. (2021), [*A Critical Review of High Burnup Fuel Fragmentation, Relocation, and Dispersal under Loss-Of-Coolant Accident Conditions*](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/critical-review-high-burnup-fuel-fragmentation-relocation-and-dispersal-under-loss); C. McKinney et al. (2026), *Identifying microstructures susceptible to pulverization in commercially irradiated high burnup UO₂ under LOCA conditions*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156853](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156853).

title: Fragment relocation and dispersal after cladding deformation
open: Predict the amount and distribution of fragmented fuel relocating within, or leaving, a deforming rod. Distinguish particle-size, restraint, gas-flow, and evolving-opening effects using integral irradiated-fuel measurements.
status: The 2022 TREAT/SATS experiment plan targets inadequately studied integral thermomechanics. Surrogate-particle studies provide partial evidence but do not establish irradiated-fuel behavior alone.
why: Relocation changes local heat generation and cooling after fuel damage.
key_works: C. B. Jensen et al. (2022), *Combined TREAT-LOC and SATS LOCA Experiment Plan: Integral LOCA Experiments on High-Burnup Fuels*, [DOI:10.2172/2352619](https://doi.org/10.2172/2352619).

title: Repeated fuel cracking, healing, and contact conductance
open: Predict crack opening, partial healing, and fragment contact across repeated power cycles together with heat-conduction effects. Reproduce time-resolved crack patterns, temperatures, and mechanical contact rather than only a final image.
status: Dedicated separate-effects UO₂ cracking experiments were reported in 2021. Transfer to irradiated, repeatedly cycled pellets remains incomplete.
why: Crack history controls temperatures and pellet–cladding mechanical loading.
key_works: S. Patnaik, B. W. Spencer, E. Roberts, T. M. Besmann, and T. W. Knight (2021), *Separate-Effects Tests for Studying Temperature-Gradient-Driven Cracking in UO₂ Pellets*, [DOI:10.1080/00295639.2021.1932223](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295639.2021.1932223).

title: In-pile versus post-irradiation thermal conductivity
open: Quantify conductivity contributions from point defects disappearing after shutdown or during laboratory measurement. Use matched in-pile and post-irradiation measurements to recover actual operating conductivity versus fission rate, temperature, and recovery time.
status: Ferrigno et al. (2023) coupled rate theory with phonon transport and identified a systematic distinction. Subsequent models examine consequences for accelerated irradiation.
why: Post-irradiation measurements can misrepresent operating-fuel temperature.
key_works: J. Ferrigno, S. Adnan, and M. Khafizov (2023), *Influence of point defect accumulation on in-pile thermal conductivity degradation: Fuel rod defect distribution and deviation between in-pile and post irradiation thermal conductivity*, [accepted manuscript](https://www.osti.gov/pages/servlets/purl/2424993).

title: Oxygen redistribution during rapid power changes
open: Determine oxygen transport and local chemical potential during transients when diffusion, temperature gradients, and evolving fission-product phases compete. Predict spatially resolved oxidation states and phase changes during independent ramps.
status: Introïni et al. (2025) coupled oxygen transport to the TAF-ID thermodynamic database and applied it to doped fuel. Transient chemical-state validation remains a distinct limitation.
why: Oxygen redistribution changes phase stability and chemical interactions at the fuel boundary.
key_works: C. Introïni, J. Sercombe, C. Guéneau, and B. Sundman (2025), *Modeling oxygen transport in Cr doped UO₂ fuel with the TAF-ID during power transients*, [journal article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022311524004537).

title: Chromium–fission-product secondary phases in real fuel
open: Determine which chromium–lanthanide secondary phases form in irradiated doped fuel, their locations, and effects on grain-boundary transport. Check model-material predictions against real-fuel phase fractions and oxidation states.
status: Shirokiy et al. (2026) identified chromium-containing perovskite-like phases in model materials and tested radiation response. Extrapolation to the full irradiated inventory remains unresolved.
why: A beneficial fresh-fuel dopant can change later microstructure and transport pathways.
key_works: D. Shirokiy et al. (2026), *Speciation and radiation stability of Cr and Ln “Grey-Phases” within Cr-doped (Ln,U)O₂ spent fuel model materials*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-026-00752-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-026-00752-5).

title: Separating grain-size and diffusivity benefits of doped fuel
open: Quantify when larger grains improve gas retention enough to offset dopant-induced changes in xenon diffusivity. Use matched irradiations varying grain size and chemical state independently, predicting steady release and transient response.
status: Cooper et al. (2021) connected atomistic chemistry to engineering gas-release models. Competing effects motivate dedicated separate-effects irradiation studies.
why: Qualification requires causal evidence for improved performance under particular conditions.
key_works: M. W. D. Cooper et al. (2021), *Fission gas diffusion and release for Cr₂O₃-doped UO₂: From the atomic to the engineering scale*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2020.152590](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2020.152590).

title: Fuel–cladding bond formation and debonding
open: Predict formation, strength, and rupture of chemically modified bonds between oxide fuel and cladding. Link interface chemistry to cohesive strength and heat transfer, including evolution after debonding.
status: Bonding has been observed for decades. Pontillon et al.’s 2025 heat-treatment study provides controlled interface experiments beyond fixed-friction contact assumptions.
why: Bonding changes heat flow and mechanical stress transferred to cladding.
key_works: Y. Pontillon, L. Desgranges, and J. Sercombe (2025), *Study of pellet-clad bonding using heat treatment of axially cut slices of PWR fuel rod*, [journal article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S002231152400641X).

title: Thoria gas-release transferability
open: Establish how grain size, pore connectivity, and irradiation-generated defects govern gas release from thoria-based fuels during steady operation and transients. Determine which UO₂ mechanisms transfer and which require thoria-specific physics.
status: Canadian irradiation and examination campaigns provide empirical comparisons. The 2021 DME-176/DME-221 analysis is a baseline, rather than comprehensive transient validation.
why: Thorium assessments need fuel-performance evidence beyond neutronic feasibility.
key_works: A. Barry (2021), *Experimental measurements to evaluate the effects of fuel microstructure on fission gas release in thoria*, [journal article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0306454920306290).

title: Hydrothermally stable high-conductivity silicide fuel
open: Demonstrate silicide-based fuel retaining its conductivity advantage while resisting rapid degradation in reactor-relevant water. Require survival under irradiation and coolant contact without relying on perfectly intact cladding.
status: Migdisov et al. (2021) established instability of the protective surface phase on U₃Si₂ in elevated-temperature aqueous conditions. A robust remedy remains open.
why: High conductivity is insufficient if a small cladding defect causes severe fuel degradation.
key_works: A. Migdisov et al. (2021), *Instability of U₃Si₂ in pressurized water media at elevated temperatures*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-021-00504-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-021-00504-3).

title: Uranium-nitride corrosion under radiolytic coolant chemistry
open: Determine whether uranium nitride’s response to radiation-generated oxidants can be predicted from ordinary water-corrosion tests. Obtain realistic surface-evolution and temperature-dependent evidence under combined irradiation and water exposure.
status: Bright et al. (2018) found different relative corrosion behavior for UN, U₂N₃, and UO₂ in peroxide solutions. That resolves a proxy comparison, while reactor-condition stability remains unestablished.
why: Nitride fuel viability depends on behavior following coolant contact.
key_works: E. Lawrence Bright et al. (2018), *Comparing the Corrosion of Uranium Nitride and Uranium Dioxide Surfaces with H₂O₂*, [arXiv:1810.12156](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.12156).

title: Nitride breakaway swelling
open: Predict accelerated-swelling onset in uranium nitride from dislocation-bubble populations, gas diffusivity, and vacancy transport. Blindly predict histories crossing the transition and validate bubble populations as well as total swelling.
status: Rizk et al. (2025) proposed a multiscale explanation and evaluated two integral fuel-pin cases. Wider validation remains necessary.
why: Abrupt swelling increases can erase otherwise attractive performance margins.
key_works: J. T. Rizk et al. (2025), *Mechanistic nuclear fuel performance modeling of uranium nitride*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.155604](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.155604).

title: Metallic-fuel constituent redistribution with evolving porosity
open: Predict radial constituent redistribution while pores grow, connect, and admit coolant or bond material. Jointly reproduce composition profiles, phase boundaries, and temperatures without compensating fits.
status: Redistribution has a substantial legacy database. Jung et al. (2025) explicitly coupled porosity and sodium infiltration to phase-field calculations, demonstrating sensitivity rather than universal closure.
why: Redistribution changes conductivity, local phase stability, and mechanical response.
key_works: W. Jung, J.-S. Kim, and K. Chang (2025), *Investigating constituent redistribution in U-Zr metallic fuels: A phase-field approach incorporating porosity and sodium infiltration*, [DOI:10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111679](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111679).

title: Metallic-fuel chemical attack of cladding
open: Predict chemically weakened cladding depth from interfacial layers, transported fission products, and temperature history. Test predictions at intermediate conditions and along full-length irradiated pins.
status: Salvato et al. (2024) compared two irradiated conditions and obtained useful model agreement, while identifying missing intermediate-condition and prototypic-length evidence.
why: Chemical attack can limit fuel lifetime even when bulk swelling is acceptable.
key_works: D. Salvato et al. (2024), *The effect of temperature and burnup on U-10Zr metallic fuel chemical interaction with HT-9: A SEM-EDS study*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154928](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154928).

title: Silver transport through apparently intact silicon carbide
open: Determine the relative roles of grain boundaries, nanopore trapping, irradiation defects, and chemically assisted pathways in silver escape through intact TRISO silicon carbide. Predict release across independently characterized coating microstructures.
status: An enduring coated-fuel puzzle. AbdulHameed et al.’s 2025 preprint required nanopore trapping to reconcile a grain-boundary transport model with measurements.
why: Silver release creates contamination and maintenance burdens despite otherwise effective containment.
key_works: M. AbdulHameed et al. (2025), *Modeling of silver transport in cubic SiC: Integrating molecular dynamics, bounds averaging, and uncertainty quantification*, [arXiv:2508.14325](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14325).

title: Multielement chemical corrosion of TRISO coatings
open: Predict silicon-carbide degradation when palladium acts with other metallic fission products. Relate local chemistry and boundary structure to reaction-front motion in irradiated coatings and subsequent retention.
status: Separate-effects work has progressively resolved individual reactions. Wei et al. (2024) showed why palladium–ruthenium interactions require explicit treatment.
why: Multielement attack can create pathways absent from single-species tests.
key_works: K. Wei et al. (2024), *Unravelling the impact of palladium on ruthenium-induced corrosion of SiC coatings in TRISO particles*, [DOI:10.1016/j.corsci.2024.112545](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.corsci.2024.112545).

title: TRISO failure probabilities in the extreme tail
open: Predict rare particle failures from joint distributions of coating geometry, defects, properties, and irradiation history. Validate correlated defects and non-spherical damage without inferring arbitrarily small failure rates from small zero-failure samples.
status: Jiang et al. (2021) implemented statistical failure analysis and multidimensional corrections in BISON. Population-tail validation beyond tested configurations remains open.
why: Whole-core retention depends on rare failures among enormous particle populations.
key_works: W. Jiang et al. (2021), *TRISO particle fuel performance and failure analysis with BISON*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2021.152795](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2021.152795).

title: Irradiation-assisted stress-corrosion initiation distributions
open: Predict crack-incubation distributions in neutron-irradiated stainless steel from boundary chemistry, localized deformation, oxide penetration, stress, and coolant history. Identify variables transferring between alloy heats without separate fitted lifetime curves.
status: Investigated since the 1960s. Was et al. (2024) substantially clarified initiation mechanisms; quantitative lifetime transfer and variability are the narrower remaining targets.
why: Inspection intervals depend on crack initiation as well as growth.
key_works: G. S. Was et al. (2024), *How irradiation promotes intergranular stress corrosion crack initiation*, [DOI:10.1016/j.pmatsci.2024.101255](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pmatsci.2024.101255).

title: Late-life manganese–nickel–silicon precipitation
open: Predict precipitation and hardening during extended vessel exposure when low flux, alloy composition, and thermal aging interact. Establish when accelerated irradiation reproduces surveillance-steel precipitates and embrittlement without empirical compensation.
status: Almirall et al. (2024) characterized nine commercial steels at extended-life fluences and tested models. Extrapolation across low-flux, long-duration histories remains a qualification problem.
why: These precipitates can change the usable lifetime of reactor vessels.
key_works: N. Almirall et al. (2024), *Irradiation microstructures and hardening in commercial nuclear reactor pressure vessel steels at high extended life fluence*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S258915292400053X).

title: Miniature-specimen fracture transfer
open: Infer component-scale fracture toughness and lower tails from miniature specimens when weld heterogeneity, irradiation, and crack-tip constraint differ. Validate transfer on withheld irradiated materials beyond mean transition-temperature agreement.
status: FRACTESUS reported substantial round-robin evidence in 2024, including unexpected transition behavior in two test series. Irradiated and heterogeneous transfer remains the target.
why: Surveillance material is scarce and destructive sampling of operating vessels is limited.
key_works: F. Obermeier et al. (2024), *PROJECT FRACTESUS: Fracture toughness round robin on a high copper weld using miniature C(T) specimens—results and discussion*, [DOI:10.5281/zenodo.13254530](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13254530).

title: Ion-to-neutron damage equivalence
open: Determine which combinations of displacement rate, implanted gases, temperature, and starting microstructure make ion irradiation reproduce neutron-induced mechanical degradation. Identify failure boundaries for the equivalence rather than assuming equal displacement dose suffices.
status: Song et al. (2024) extended damage in reactor-irradiated 316 steel using ions and obtained semi-quantitative microstructural agreement. Universal property transfer was not demonstrated.
why: Credible acceleration could shorten materials qualification by years.
key_works: M. Song, K. G. Field, K. Sun, and G. S. Was (2024), *Extending damage accumulation of commercial reactor irradiated 316 stainless steel with ion irradiation*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154989](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154989).

title: Dislocation-loop contributions to irradiation creep
open: Quantify how stress-biased loop motion, climb, and defect absorption combine into macroscopic irradiation creep under changing stress. Connect observed loop trajectories to strain without assuming one mechanism dominates across dose and temperature.
status: Ding et al. (2024) measured loop motion in situ under simultaneous stress and irradiation. Bridging those observations to bulk constitutive laws remains incomplete.
why: Small accumulated strains change alignment, clearances, and load sharing over decades.
key_works: Y. Ding et al. (2024), *Quantitative in-situ investigation of dislocation loop motion in Fe9Cr1.5W ferritic/martensitic steel under the coupling effects of constant stress and irradiation*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S002231152400268X).

title: Recovering bulk swelling from surface-biased experiments
open: Infer bulk cavity nucleation and swelling from shallow ion-irradiated layers while separating surface, grain-boundary, and impurity-sink effects. Demonstrate prediction of independent thick-specimen or neutron data.
status: Li et al. (2024) resolved temperature- and rate-dependent void-denuded regions in iron. These measurements demonstrate why averaging a surface layer can conceal bulk behavior.
why: Surface bias can reverse apparent rankings of radiation-resistant alloys.
key_works: Y. Li et al. (2024), *The dependence on displacement rate and temperature of near-surface void-denuding in self-ion irradiated pure polycrystalline and single-crystal iron*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022311524003647).

title: Helium-dependent creep-crack growth
open: Predict creep-crack growth when irradiation-generated helium changes grain-boundary cavitation and ductility. Establish transferable relations between helium distribution, constraint, history, and crack advance across alloy families.
status: Petkov and Juan (2025) assessed methods against irradiated Nimonic PE16 tie-bar tests. This material-specific validation does not settle other helium populations or loading histories.
why: Components can become fracture-limited before conventional creep-rupture predictions indicate failure.
key_works: M. Petkov and P.-A. Juan (2025), *Validation of assessment methods for creep crack growth rates in irradiated components from Nimonic PE16 Tie-Bar tests*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0029549324007817).

title: Oxide-nanocluster survival under cascades
open: Predict whether strengthening nanoclusters dissolve, coarsen, or renucleate under a specified cascade spectrum. Explain number-density evolution while also predicting size and retained strengthening.
status: The NSUF Patki–Wharry project builds on neutron, proton, and ion studies. Its stated unresolved issue is why number density responds differently from particle size.
why: Oxide-dispersion-strengthened steels depend on persistent nanoscale obstacles.
key_works: P. Patki and J. Wharry, *Role of Irradiation Damage Cascade Descriptors on ODS and Model ODS Nanocluster Evolution*, [NSUF project and publications, accessed 2026](https://nsuf.inl.gov/Home/Project/1757).

title: Simultaneous versus sequential irradiation–creep–fatigue
open: Determine when testing after irradiation gives the same damage evolution as simultaneous irradiation and cyclic loading. Identify regimes where ongoing defect production invalidates sequential qualification.
status: Michigan’s 2024 project explicitly compares both routes in Grade 91 and Alloy 709. Broadly validated testing equivalence remains unavailable.
why: Separate irradiation and mechanical tests dominate databases but can miss coupling.
key_works: K. G. Field’s NOME Lab (2024), [*Mechanism Driven Evaluations of Sequential and Simultaneous Irradiation-Creep-Fatigue Testing*](https://www.nome.engin.umich.edu/project/irrcf/).

title: Long-dwell creep–fatigue in impure helium
open: Predict Alloy 617 cracking during long dwells when helium impurities cause changing oxidation, carburization, or decarburization. Validate combined chemical and multiaxial mechanical histories beyond single-temperature laboratory cycles.
status: Carroll et al. (2011) established environmental and hold-time effects. Material acceptance does not eliminate this lifetime-extrapolation problem.
why: High-temperature exchangers must sustain years of thermal cycling and dwell.
key_works: L. J. Carroll, C. Cabet, R. Madland, and R. N. Wright (2011), *Creep and environmental effects on the high temperature creep-fatigue behavior of alloy 617*, [INL publication](https://inl.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/creep-and-environmental-effects-on-the-high-temperature-creep-fat-2/).

title: When irradiation accelerates or suppresses salt corrosion
open: Establish when irradiation increases, decreases, or leaves unchanged intergranular corrosion in molten salts. Separate defect-enhanced alloy transport from radiolysis and chemical-potential changes, validating the sign across radiation species and salt conditions.
status: Zhou et al. (2019) observed proton irradiation decelerating Ni–Cr corrosion, disproving a simple assumption that irradiation always worsens attack. General operating boundaries remain open.
why: Unirradiated corrosion tests may misrepresent in-reactor wall loss.
key_works: W. Zhou et al. (2019), *Proton Irradiation-Decelerated Intergranular Corrosion of Ni-Cr Alloys in Molten Salt*, [arXiv:1911.11798](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11798).

title: Nonisothermal salt-loop corrosion and deposition
open: Predict coupled hot-region dissolution and cold-region deposition in circulating multimetal salt systems over long operation. Close mass balances while tracking chemistry, surface composition, deposited particles, and local transport.
status: Kim et al. (2024) demonstrated corrosion-product migration and cold-leg deposition in a 500-hour chloride loop. Static coupon rates do not predict the complete redistribution process.
why: Material can disappear from one component and obstruct or contaminate another.
key_works: T. Kim et al. (2024), *Corrosion Behavior of Candidate Structural Materials for Molten Salt Reactors in Flowing NaCl-MgCl₂*, [DOI:10.1155/2024/2883918](https://doi.org/10.1155/2024/2883918).

title: Durable molten-salt reference electrodes
open: Maintain a traceable electrochemical reference through months of flowing-salt irradiation, thermal cycling, and composition changes. Demonstrate bounded drift and distinguish electrode degradation from genuine redox changes.
status: Yuan et al. (2025) demonstrated a MgMn₂O₄ solid-state reference with approximately 100 hours of stable open-circuit behavior. Component-lifetime stability remains a different target.
why: Chemistry control requires knowing whether the sensor or the salt changed.
key_works: Y. Yuan et al. (2025), *A MgMn₂O₄-Based Solid State Reference Electrode for High-Temperature Molten Salts*, [DOI:10.1149/1945-7111/adcaee](https://doi.org/10.1149/1945-7111/adcaee).

title: Tellurium embrittlement of candidate salt-reactor steels
open: Relate tellurium activity and grain-boundary uptake in realistic salts to crack initiation and ductility loss in 316H steel. Determine whether laboratory exposures predict damage under stress, irradiation, and evolving chemistry.
status: Tellurium attack affected historical nickel-alloy programmes. Reyes et al. (2025) found embrittlement in initial 316H exposures and identified realistic salt testing as unfinished.
why: Acceptable average corrosion can coexist with brittle boundary failure.
key_works: L. K. Reyes et al. (2025), *Initial Studies of Tellurium Embrittlement in 316H Stainless Steel*, [DOI:10.1080/00295450.2024.2421690](https://doi.org/10.1080/00295450.2024.2421690).

title: Protective-oxide loss and repair in flowing lead alloys
open: Predict whether damaged oxide films repair or undergo continuing erosion–corrosion in lead or lead–bismuth coolant. Resolve oxygen transport, impingement, oxide growth, spallation, and substrate changes over repeated transients.
status: Li, Wang, and Wang (2024) measured velocity- and geometry-sensitive attack during long flowing-LBE exposures. Self-repair across changing service flow fields remains uncertain.
why: Protection depends on the weakest damaged region, not average oxide thickness.
key_works: J. Li, Y. Wang, and X. Wang (2024), *Erosion–corrosion behaviors of P91 steel in high-velocity flowing lead–bismuth eutectic*, [DOI:10.13374/j.issn2095-9389.2023.11.28.005](https://doi.org/10.13374/j.issn2095-9389.2023.11.28.005).

title: Liquid-metal embrittlement initiation thresholds
open: Determine crack-initiation thresholds for steels in liquid lead alloys as oxide continuity, exposure, strain rate, and temperature change. Explain when liquid access to a stressed boundary becomes a propagating crack.
status: Zhang, Qin, and Long (2025) mapped exposure and strain-rate effects in T91. Transfer to multiaxial service histories remains unresolved.
why: Tensile strength in air does not establish fracture resistance in coolant.
key_works: J. Zhang, B. Qin, and B. Long (2025), *Study on Liquid Metal Embrittlement Susceptibility of T91 Exposed to Liquid Lead-Bismuth Eutectic*, [DOI:10.3390/met15020206](https://doi.org/10.3390/met15020206).

title: Permeation barriers that survive reactor service
open: Demonstrate retention of a tritium-permeation barrier’s suppression factor after irradiation, thermal cycling, substrate creep, and aggressive chemistry. Measure transport through defects and joints, including transferability of hydrogen-surrogate results.
status: Liang et al. (2023) developed an Al₂O₃/Ni–Al barrier for molten-salt applications. Long-duration, defect-sensitive qualification remains open.
why: Small damaged areas can dominate plant-wide isotope leakage and maintenance burdens.
key_works: C. Liang et al. (2023), *An Al₂O₃/Ni–Al tritium permeation barrier coating for the potential application in thorium-based molten salt reactor*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0042207X2300307X).

title: Hydride-network reorientation and ductility
open: Predict how thermal and stress histories transform dispersed zirconium hydrides into connected crack paths. Link texture, precipitation history, and three-dimensional connectivity to ductility without a universal radial-hydride threshold.
status: Kang et al. (2026) compared reorientation and ring-compression ductility in two ZIRLO conditions. A transferable history-to-fracture law remains incomplete.
why: Redistribution of existing hydrogen can change previously acceptable cladding’s fracture behavior.
key_works: S. Kang, M. Gussev, M. Billone, and A. Motta (2026), *Study of hydride reorientation and ductility of SRA ZIRLO and PRXA ZIRLO using ring compression testing*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.156225](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.156225).

title: Irradiated niobium precipitates and zirconium corrosion
open: Predict how irradiation changes niobium-rich precipitates and matrix chemistry, and how these changes alter oxide growth and hydrogen uptake. Validate the causal chain under neutron exposure.
status: Wang et al. (2026) resolved proton-induced precipitate transformations and improved subsequent autoclave corrosion resistance. Transfer to simultaneous neutron irradiation and corrosion, hydrogen uptake, and broader histories remains open.
why: Could explain why nominally similar cladding alloys diverge during long service.
key_works: P. Wang et al. (2026), *Effect of proton irradiation on Zr-1Nb alloy: Microstructure, microchemistry, and corrosion*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022311526003363).

title: Chromium-coated cladding after cumulative damage
open: Predict protection after chromium coatings accumulate irradiation damage, deformation cracks, interdiffusion, and oxidation. Determine which defects remain isolated and which initiate rapid substrate attack during subsequent steam transients.
status: Jung et al. (2025) resolved coating-microstructure effects in high-temperature steam. Fresh-coating tests do not establish equivalent protection after a full irradiation history.
why: Accident tolerance must survive normal service before it can help during an accident.
key_works: T. S. Jung, H. Jang, Y. K. Cho, and D. Jang (2025), *Degradation behavior of chromium-coated zirconium cladding under 1200°C steam oxidation according to coating microstructure*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022311524004616).

title: Irradiated silicon-carbide composite hermeticity
open: Maintain and predict gas tightness of complete SiC composite tubes and joints under heat flux, irradiation, and thermal cycling. Connect microcracks and joint damage to measured leakage and sealing-layer lifetime.
status: Koyanagi et al. (2024) found radial-heat-flux irradiation could compromise composite-tube hermeticity while tested monolithic tubes retained it. Mitigation requires lifecycle validation.
why: Mechanical strength alone does not establish fission-product containment.
key_works: T. Koyanagi et al. (2024), *Hermeticity of SiC/SiC composite and monolithic SiC tubes irradiated under radial high-heat flux*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2023.154784](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2023.154784).

title: Graphite dimensional turnaround across grades
open: Predict irradiation-driven shrinkage, expansion turnaround, and creep for a new graphite grade from its initial pore and crystallite structure. Provide calibrated uncertainty beyond measured grades and dose ranges.
status: Dhulipala et al. (2025) calibrated four irradiated-property models across five grades, including model discrepancy. Out-of-grade and extended-dose prediction remains a stronger target.
why: Core geometry and load paths evolve with graphite dimensions and stiffness.
key_works: S. L. N. Dhulipala et al. (2025), *Bayesian calibration of irradiated graphite property models under high temperatures*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-025-00710-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-025-00710-7).

title: Coupled irradiation and moisture damage in concrete
open: Predict cracking and stiffness loss when aggregate radiation-induced expansion interacts with paste drying, radiolysis, creep, and moisture transport. Validate coupling from minerals through composites to thick structures with exposure gradients.
status: Qi et al. (2025) investigated irradiated mineral analogues of aggregates. A validated structural-scale lifetime model combining constituent damage remains unfinished.
why: Biological shields and supports can age through mechanisms absent from ordinary civil-engineering tests.
key_works: Z. Qi et al. (2025), *Investigation of ion irradiation effects on mineral analogues of concrete aggregates*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022311524006408).

title: Critical-heat-flux prediction across geometries
open: Predict boiling-crisis onset for withheld rod-bundle geometries and surface conditions, with uncertainty valid outside the training database. Separate physical scaling from correlations encoding particular facilities or campaigns.
status: Decades of correlations provide useful predictions. Furlong et al. (2025) integrated conventional and hybrid machine learning into CTF and tested selected datasets; broader transfer remains unproven.
why: Heat-flux limits constrain power density and safety margins.
key_works: A. Furlong, X. Zhao, R. Salko, and X. Wu (2025), *Deployment of Traditional and Hybrid Machine Learning for Critical Heat Flux Prediction in the CTF Thermal Hydraulics Code*, [arXiv:2505.14701](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14701).

title: Disturbance-wave control of intermittent dryout
open: Predict dry-patch formation and rewetting from disturbance-wave statistics in high-pressure annular steam–water flow with spacers and nonuniform heating. Transfer mechanisms between fluids and geometries without refitting local closures.
status: Morse et al. (2024) directly characterized intermittent dryout and proposed mechanistic models using a transparent refrigerant experiment. Reactor-condition transfer remains the narrower open problem.
why: Local dry patches determine temperature excursions before complete film disappearance.
key_works: R. W. Morse et al. (2024), *A new paradigm for the role of disturbance waves on film dryout and wall heat transfer in annular two-phase flow*, [DOI:10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2023.124812](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2023.124812).

title: Identifiable wall-boiling heat partition
open: Determine evaporation, transient conduction, and convection contributions independently enough to identify model parameters. Test whether matching wall temperature conceals compensating bubble-size, departure-frequency, nucleation, or coalescence errors.
status: Favre et al. (2025) examined physical consistency and validation of heat-flux-partition models. Simultaneous closure-level validation across pressures and surface conditions remains incomplete.
why: Correct total heat flux can coexist with incorrect void distributions and boiling margins.
key_works: L. Favre et al. (2025), *On physical considerations regarding development and validation of Heat Flux Partitioning models: Application to vertical boiling flows simulations*, [arXiv:2507.12478](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12478).

title: High-pressure bubble-population closure data
open: Measure joint bubble-size, velocity, coalescence, breakup, and condensation statistics in high-pressure subcooled boiling well enough to distinguish interfacial-area closures. Test radial distributions and transient heat transfer beyond average void fraction.
status: Chavasse-Frétaz et al. (2024) analyzed high-pressure two-fluid simulations and energy budgets. Independently resolved population dynamics remain a limiting validation input.
why: Interfacial area controls momentum and energy exchange between coolant phases.
key_works: E. Chavasse-Frétaz, A. Burlot, G. Bois, and C. Colin (2024), *Physical Insights into High-Pressure Subcooled Boiling Through Two-Fluid Simulations*, [SSRN:5017563](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5017563).

title: Direct turbulent-heat-flux measurements in liquid metals
open: Measure simultaneous velocity–temperature fluctuations in opaque liquid metals with bandwidth and resolution sufficient to recover turbulent heat-flux components. Produce uncertainty-qualified mixed- and natural-convection data discriminating isotropic and anisotropic models.
status: Carlesi’s 2025 thesis obtained useful mean-field agreement but reported fluctuation-measurement limitations preventing reliable direct turbulent-heat-flux quantification in Galinstan.
why: Low-Prandtl-number transport cannot be validated solely through mean temperatures.
key_works: T. Carlesi (2025), *Development of an advanced experimental technique for the measurement of the turbulent heat flux in liquid metals*, [doctoral thesis](https://researchportal.sckcen.be/en/publications/development-of-an-advanced-experimental-technique-for-the-measure/).
